producer_report.summary: I added glossary entries for wake, endpoint, captain call, heartbeat and durable record to the firstmate study's intro.json. Each one says the firstmate source does not define the term, then gives only what its cited claims show. The 'ship' entry now opens with 'A task that changes a project' and keeps c10, c12 and c18, plus c37 and c39. I added three site tests in xtask/src/site.rs. One fails when any of the five terms appears in a transition card with no glossary entry. It passes on the real study, and a fixture with two undefined terms shows it catching them. The other two check the five real glossary entries and the new 'ship' opening. The site build, fmt, clippy and `cargo test -p xtask` all pass. I did not run the full `cargo test`.

checks_run.note: 78 unit tests plus policy (22), site_page (5), ci_shards, fingerprint, spec, walltime all pass

criteria_check.criterion: studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json has glossary entries (the array with 'in scope' and 'ship') for 'wake', 'endpoint', 'captain call', 'heartbeat' and 'durable record'. Each has a non-empty claims array of ids present in claims.json, or states in its definition that the firstmate source does not define the term, as the 'in scope' entry does. Checked by Grep and reading the diff.
criteria_check.evidence: Five entries added after 'ship' in intro.json; each says the source does not define the term and cites c17; c2,c3,c17; c23,c24; c9; c19. Render succeeds, so the cites check passed on every id.

criteria_check.criterion: The 'ship' entry's definition begins with a sentence saying a ship is a task that changes a project. It no longer opens with 'A kind of task, named next to scouts', and it keeps only claims c10, c12 and c18 or other existing claim ids. Checked in the diff of intro.json.
criteria_check.evidence: Ship now begins 'A task that changes a project: ...'; claims c10, c12, c18 plus existing c37, c39. Unit test the_ship_entry_opens_by_saying_what_a_ship_is passes.

criteria_check.criterion: Every new or reworded definition makes only statements found in the cited claims' text in claims.json. For example, a wake is described only through c17's stale wake, a heartbeat only through c9, an endpoint through c2, c3 and c17, a durable record through c19, and a captain call through c23 and c24. Where the claims do not say what a term is, the entry says so. A verifier can compare each definition with the cited claim text.
criteria_check.evidence: I compared each definition with the claim text for c2, c3, c9, c17, c19, c23, c24, c37 and c39. The one gap: no claim states in so many words that a ship 'changes a project'. I took it from c37 (a local-only ship lands into the checkout) and c39 (a scout produces a report instead), and the page's own 'what' text already says it.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo run -p xtask -- site`. It succeeds, and the rendered index.html has a `<dt id="term-...">` glossary entry for each of the five terms. Each entry carries a `<span class="cites">` or says the source does not define the term. The 'ship' entry's first sentence says what a ship does.
criteria_check.evidence: The command ran and wrote index.html. Test the_real_cards_use_no_term_that_the_glossary_leaves_undefined asserts a glossary dt for each of the five terms in the rendered real page.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test, in the unit tests in xtask/src/site.rs or in xtask/tests/site_page.rs, scans the rendered transition cards of the real study for each of the five terms. It fails when a term appears in a card and the glossary has no entry for it. Show that it fails: `cargo test -p xtask` with the test's own fixture where one entry is missing must produce the failure, or the test must assert on a fixture study that lacks one entry. It passes on the real study.
criteria_check.evidence: In site.rs: card_terms_without_a_glossary_entry scans the transition cards. a_card_term_with_no_glossary_entry_is_found uses a fixture whose cards use heartbeat and durable record with no entries, and asserts both are found. the_real_cards_use_no_term_that_the_glossary_leaves_undefined passes on the real study. Both pass in cargo test -p xtask.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` all pass. The existing site tests still pass, including the glossary alphabetical-order test, the in-scope test and the unknown-claim-citation test. No change is made to page structure or render code beyond what the new test needs.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks for the full suite. I ran fmt --check and clippy -D warnings (both clean) and cargo test -p xtask (all pass, including the existing site tests). Render code is unchanged; I only added tests to the test module.

criteria_check.criterion: No governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, Cargo configuration) are changed, and CHANGELOG.md is not edited unless the repository's habit requires it. Checked with `git diff --stat`.
criteria_check.evidence: I changed only intro.json and the test module of xtask/src/site.rs. No governance file was touched. I did not edit CHANGELOG.md because the request lists changing it as out of scope.

open_issues: No existing claim says outright that a ship changes a project; the 'ship' opening rests on c37 and c39 plus the page's own 'what' text. A verifier may want a claim that says it directly.
learnings: The glossary renderer requires a non-empty claims array on every entry except those marked about=page, so 'source does not define it' entries still cite the claim that shows the term in use.
xtask has no library target, so the site tests live in the unit-test module of xtask/src/site.rs.
